facts.text: The red-browed finch is easily recognised by a bright red stripe above the eye and a bright red rump.
facts.quote: The species is distinguished by the bright red stripe above the eye and bright red rump.

facts.text: It is highly sociable, usually appearing in small flocks of 10 to 20 individuals.
facts.quote: The red-browed finch is highly sociable and is usually seen in small flocks of 10 to 20 individuals.

facts.text: When disturbed, the whole flock disperses while cheeping, then re-congregates nearby.
facts.quote: When disturbed, the whole flock will disperse, cheeping, and re-congregate nearby.

facts.text: The finch mostly eats grass and sedge seed but will happily feed on many non-native seeds.
facts.quote: N. temporalis is a seed eater, living mostly on grass and sedge seed, but will happily feed on many non-native seeds.

facts.text: Wild birds will even enter large-mesh aviaries in suburban areas to eat seed.
facts.quote: Wild birds will even enter large-mesh aviaries in suburban areas to eat seed, given the opportunity.

facts.text: It builds a large domed nest with a side entrance, woven from grass and small twigs, usually 2–3 metres above the ground.
facts.quote: The red-browed finch builds a large domed nest with a side entrance, woven from grass and small twigs. Nests are usually built 2–3 metres (6.6–9.8 ft) above the ground in dense shrubs.

facts.text: Both parents share nest building, incubation, and feeding of the young.
facts.quote: Both parents share nest building, incubation of the eggs, and feed the young together.

facts.text: Four to six white eggs are laid per clutch two or three times per year, between October and April.
facts.quote: Four to six white eggs are laid per clutch two or three times per year, between October and April.

facts.text: In captivity it sometimes hybridises with the star finch, crimson finch, and zebra finch.
facts.quote: The red-browed finch will sometimes hybridise with the star finch, crimson finch, and zebra finch if kept together in captivity.

facts.text: The species is listed as being of least concern on the IUCN Red List.
facts.quote: The species is listed as being of least concern on the IUCN Red List.
